description: IW(k) is breadth-first search with *novelty pruning*. Each state is described by integer *features*, such as the facts that hold in it, and the *novelty* of a state is the size of the smallest set of its features that no earlier state had all at once. IW(k) drops every non-goal state with novelty greater than `k`, so it expands at most `O(n^k)` states for `n` features, however large the state space is. The *width* of a problem is, roughly, the smallest `k` for which IW(k) finds a shortest plan (all actions cost 1); with a larger width, IW(k) can fail. *Iterated width* (`iterated_width`) runs IW(1), IW(2), … until one succeeds, which suits large state spaces where no heuristic is at hand.
